name: Welcoming Vampire
oracle_text:
Flying
Whenever one or more other creatures you control with power 2 or less enter, draw a card. This ability triggers only once each turn.
blocked_sentences: Whenever one or more other creatures you control with power 2 or less enter, draw a card. This ability triggers only once each turn.

needs.what: a per-turn cap declared on a triggered ability's trigger -- e.g. `"trigger": {"event": "permanent_enters", "filter": {...}, "max_per_turn": 1}` -- so that once the ability has triggered that many times this turn, later matching events do not queue it at all. It has to be enforced where triggers are collected (`triggers.collect`/`_matches`), counted per (source object, ability index) in the turn ledger and reset at cleanup, and it must count *triggers*, not resolutions: a trigger that is countered or removed from the stack has still spent the turn's allowance
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `once_each_turn` exists on `Ability` but is an *activation* restriction, and `loader._compile_ability` raises `DslError` outright when it appears on anything that is not an activated ability ("'activate_steps' and 'once_each_turn' restrict *activating*, so they only mean anything on an activated ability"); `legality` is the only reader, and a trigger never passes through it. `TriggerSpec`/`TriggerModel` carry only `event`, `controller`, `source`, `filter`, `condition`, `defending`, `not_cause` and `counter` -- no limiter. The two near misses say something different: `set_flag`/`{"has_flag": ...}` is a one-way word (`objects.py` clears `flags` only on a zone change, never at cleanup), so it would make this once *ever* rather than once each turn; and `{"cmp": ..., "left": {"resolutions_this_turn": "self"}}` gates *resolving*, not triggering -- `ctx.resolutions` is set by `stack.resolve_top`, so the trigger still goes on the stack every time and a countered first copy would leave the allowance unspent. docs/rules-coverage.md already names `resolutions_this_turn` "the wrong number" for exactly this cap

needs.what: a way to say "whenever one or more <matching> permanents enter" -- one trigger for a whole simultaneous batch of ENTERS_BATTLEFIELD events rather than one per object. The entering permanents need to be gathered into a single event (or the queued triggers deduplicated per batch) before `collect` queues anything, with the batch exposed as a binding so an effect can still read how many entered
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `permanent_enters` maps one-to-one onto `EventType.ENTERS_BATTLEFIELD` and `triggers.fire` runs once per object, so a `{"types": ["Creature"], "controller": "you", "exclude_self": true, "power": {"op": "<=", "value": 2}}` filter queues N triggers when N small creatures enter together and draws N cards where the card draws one. `not_cause` only suppresses by zone-change cause and `condition` is evaluated per event, so neither collapses a batch. Note this need cannot be papered over by the per-turn cap above and vice versa: the cap alone still queues N triggers (only the first would do anything), and the batching alone still draws once per later enter this turn

needs.what: a trigger filter whose `power`/`toughness` comparison reads the subject's *current* characteristics as it exists on the battlefield rather than its printed ones, for "creatures you control with power 2 or less enter"
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `triggers.matches_card_filter` compares against `card.power` (the printed face) by design, because trigger subjects are frequently gone by the time the filter runs. That is right for a `dies` trigger and wrong here: a printed 1/1 that enters as a 3/3 under an anthem, or with counters from a replacement effect, would still trigger. A subject that has just entered is still on the battlefield, so the derived characteristics are available -- but the filter never asks for them, and there is no key to request the derived reading
